lastCompletedStory.title: Review round 1 fix 003: address reviewer finding

nextStoryContext: US-R1-003 fixed the reviewer's finding at test/init.test.ts:81: the 3 tests were bound to a `CAM_CONFIG_PATH` env-var seam that US-001 (this same PRD) had already made dead in production code (src/commands/init.ts reads no such variable and has no config-write path at all), so the tests could never go red no matter what init actually did. The mechanical fix note suggested driving init via `HOME` pointed at a tmpdir instead. I attempted exactly that first, then verified against real runtime behavior (not just the note's prose, per the global 'verify comments against runtime' lesson) and discovered Bun 1.3.13's `node:os` `homedir()` does NOT dynamically re-read `process.env.HOME` after process start, contrary to both Node's and Bun's own documented behavior (confirmed via WebFetch against https://bun.com/reference/node/os/homedir, which claims $HOME-based resolution) -- mutating `process.env.HOME` mid-test has zero effect on subsequent `homedir()` calls in the same process. So a HOME-redirect design would have silently reproduced the exact same defect (test bound to a seam nothing reacts to), just with a different env var. Instead I collapsed the 3 duplicate tests into 1 that snapshots the REAL (unfakeable) `~/.config/cam` directory listing before calling `runInit()` twice and asserts it is unchanged after -- this is safe on both a clean CI runner (both snapshots null) and this repo's own dev machine (which has a stale `~/.config/cam/config.toml` left over from pre-US-001 `cam init` runs, plus a legitimately-live `retry.toml` from src/retry/config.ts -- both preserved unchanged by the assertion, no false positive). This is a live, falsifiable regression guard: a future code path that writes ANY new file under `~/.config/cam/`, including at the exact old default path, would flip the snapshot diff and fail the test. Documented the Bun `homedir()` env-mutation quirk as a new scripts/cam/patterns.md bullet (option (a) child-process-with-spawn-time-env, option (b) real-value-before/after-diff -- this story used (b)) since it's a genuinely reusable gotcha for any future test needing to redirect a Bun `node:os` path function. No production src/ files touched; scope was strictly test/init.test.ts per the finding. All quality gates (typecheck, full `bun test` 5760/5760, full `bun run check:all` spine including coverage/dead-code/dup/lint/file-size/ci-parity/skip-ratchet) green.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Docs claim homedir() reads $HOME on POSIX per-call, matching Node's documented behavior. Empirically verified on Bun 1.3.13 that mutating process.env.HOME mid-process has NO effect on subsequent homedir() calls (the value is resolved once, before user JS runs). Test design was corrected to bind to the real, unfakeable homedir() result via a before/after directory snapshot instead of relying on an env-var redirect that doesn't actually work on this runtime.
